articles.title: Onboarding in Confluence: make new hires watch the right spaces automatically
articles.excerpt: A new hire should see what their team writes from day one: the team space, the handbook, the incident log. In Confluence Cloud, watching is a personal setting, so nothing happens when someone joins th…
articles.body: A new hire should see what their team writes from day one: the team space, the handbook, the incident log. In Confluence Cloud, watching is a personal setting, so nothing happens when someone joins the team. Here is what you can do with Confluence alone, and where it stops. What new hires get by default Autowatch is on by default, but it only covers pages a person creates, edits or comments on. A new hire watches nothing in the team space until they have worked on a page there. Watching a space covers all its pages and blog posts, and the person has to switch it on (or an admin does it for them, see Option 3). Watching does not give access. If the space is restricted, the new hire has to be able to see it first.
articles.author: Kayabyte

articles.title: Premia Exploit: Empty Option Pools Drained Six Vaults
articles.excerpt: Originally published at Premia Exploit: Empty Option Pools Drained Six Vaults On 1 November 2026, an attacker emptied six Premia v3 underwriter vaults on Arbitrum in two transactions sent one second a…
articles.body: Originally published at Premia Exploit: Empty Option Pools Drained Six Vaults On 1 November 2026 , an attacker emptied six Premia v3 underwriter vaults on Arbitrum in two transactions sent one second apart. The vaults lost 3.644 WBTC, 43.47 WETH, 48,479 USDC.e and 46,215 ARB , which The Defiant valued at about $437,000 . Blockaid flagged the attack while it was still running and described the method in one sentence: the attacker created empty option pools, flash-loaned capital, bought options so that vault collateral was locked into those pools, and then withdrew that collateral as liquidity. No key was stolen and no oracle was bent. The vaults did what their code allowed: they underwrote options in markets that the attacker had created a minute earlier.

articles.body: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) and structuredClone(x) are both used to deep copy an object. They do not copy the same things. I ran both on one object in Node v22.23.4 and wrote down the differences. One object, two copies Test object: a Date, undefined , NaN , Infinity , a Map, a Set, a RegExp, -0 , and an array with a hole ( [1, , 3] ). Value After JSON round trip After structuredClone new Date(0) the string '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' a Date undefined property key is gone undefined , key kept NaN , Infinity null NaN , Infinity new Map([[1, 2]]) {} a Map with 1 => 2 new Set([1]) {} a Set /a/gi {} /a/gi -0 0 -0 [1, , 3] [1, null, 3] [1, <1 empty item>, 3] 10n (BigInt) throws TypeError 10n So the JSON route silently turns a Map into {} and a Date into a string.

articles.title: Build Your Own Local Knowledge Base So an AI Agent Can Write Client Emails That Sound Like You
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I am from the aiFetchly team. Most generic AI emails fail for a simple reason: the model does not know your business. It does not know how you describe a service, which cases you accept, w…
articles.body: Disclosure: I am from the aiFetchly team. Most generic AI emails fail for a simple reason: the model does not know your business. It does not know how you describe a service, which cases you accept, what you never promise, or how you follow up. A local knowledge base fixes that — not by adding more prompts, but by giving the agent a small, curated source of truth to draw on. 1. Start with your own documents, not the whole internet Collect the material you already trust: service pages, FAQs, proposal templates, past replies you were happy with, pricing notes, and objection-handling answers. Keep it in one place and prune ruthlessly. If a document is outdated, remove it or mark it superseded. A knowledge base with 30 accurate pages beats one with 300 stale ones.

articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962.

articles.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
articles.excerpt: From a close encounter between Mars and Jupiter to dazzling Venus and elusive Mercury, November offers plenty of planetary highlights. Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
